## Summary

The 2026-08-26 `rm -rf /*` incident came from an **ad-hoc, agent-authored mutation
script** (`/tmp/mut.py`: `EP.write_text(orig.replace(old, new, 1))` then
`subprocess.run([... pytest ...])`). It never touched `scripts/mutation_gate.py`.

`e668-b496-e264-4283` sandboxes the CI mutation gate. That is worth having, but it
**does not cover the path the incident took**. The path the incident took is the
defect-seeded mutation check that `rebar-debug` and `rebar-implement` instruct agents
to perform as a routine part of TDD — and neither skill requires any sandbox.

## Evidence

- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md:786` — *"perturb the fix with a
  **defect-seeded mutation** … confirm the held-out test returns to **RED**, then
  restore the fix."*
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md:291` — *"perturb the implementation
  … A test that stays green under mutation is a tautology."*
- `grep -rilE "sandbox-exec|bwrap|bubblewrap" examples/agent-skills/` returns
  **nothing**. No skill mentions an OS sandbox anywhere.

These skills are symlinked into `~/.claude/skills/`, so the rule ships to every
operator who installs them.

## Why an inline invocation, not a dependency on the wrapper

The rule must not wait on `e668`'s `scripts/mutation_sandbox.py` landing: the skills
are the live instruction agents follow today, and the exposure is present on every
run until the rule exists. The skills therefore carry the sandbox invocation inline.
A follow-on ticket adds a reusable CLI wrapper and can simplify the skill text later.

## The invocations, in full

Both were measured today, not composed from memory.

**macOS** — the profile is written by the snippet itself, so nothing external is
referenced. Verified on macOS 26.5.2: a write outside `$SBX` was denied
(`Operation not permitted`, file absent), a write inside succeeded, and
`rm -rf <protected>/*` was denied with the target surviving.

```sh
SBX="$(mktemp -d)"
cat > "$SBX/p.sb" <<EOF
(version 1)
(allow default)
(deny file-write*)
(allow file-write*
  (subpath "$PWD")
  (subpath "$SBX")
  (literal "/dev/null") (literal "/dev/stdout") (literal "/dev/stderr"))
EOF
sandbox-exec -f "$SBX/p.sb" <your mutation test command>
```

**Linux** — verified in an `ubuntu:24.04` container: the write inside the bind
succeeded and a write outside failed with `Read-only file system`.

```sh
bwrap --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc --bind "$PWD" "$PWD" -- <your mutation test command>
```

`bwrap` presence on PATH is NOT capability: Ubuntu 23.10+ restricts unprivileged
user namespaces via AppArmor, so an installed `bwrap` can fail with "Creating new
namespace failed". Confirm it works first:

```sh
bwrap --ro-bind / / -- /bin/true || echo "bwrap cannot namespace here"
```

## When no sandbox is available

Neither mechanism present, or `bwrap` present but unable to namespace: **do not run
the mutation step against code that performs real filesystem deletion, and do not
proceed unsandboxed.** Assert on an injected seam instead — point the deletion at a
stub that records its argv and assert on what *would* have been deleted. That is a
strictly better oracle than observing a wiped directory, and it needs no sandbox.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both `rebar-debug` and `rebar-implement` require any step that perturbs code and
      then executes tests to run inside an OS sandbox denying writes outside the
      worktree and a scratch dir. Verified by
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_skill_mutation_sandbox_rule.py`.
- [ ] Each skill carries the **complete, self-contained** macOS snippet above,
      including the heredoc that writes the profile — no reference to a profile file
      whose provenance or content is unstated. Verified by the test asserting the
      `(deny file-write*)` and `sandbox-exec -f` literals are present in both files.
- [ ] Each skill carries the **complete** Linux `bwrap` invocation above, including
      `--ro-bind / /`, `--dev`, `--proc` and the `--bind "$PWD" "$PWD"` pair — not an
      abbreviated fragment. Verified by the same test.
- [ ] Each skill states that `bwrap` on PATH is not capability, and gives the
      `bwrap --ro-bind / / -- /bin/true` capability probe. Verified by the same test.
- [ ] Each skill specifies the **no-sandbox fallback**: assert on an injected seam,
      never proceed unsandboxed. Verified by the same test.
- [ ] Each skill states that a seeded defect is arbitrary code, so the run executes
      hostile code — with the 2026-08-26 outcome as the reason. Verified by the test.
- [ ] A regression test fails if either skill loses the requirement. Verified by
      removing it from one skill and observing RED.
- [ ] No existing guidance is weakened: RED-first, held-out-oracle and mutation-teeth
      discipline unchanged; the sandbox is added around them. Verified by diff review.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_skill_mutation_sandbox_rule.py` — both skills carry the
  requirement, both platform invocations, and the hostile-code framing; the test goes
  RED when the rule is removed from either file.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — green.
- `python scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` — the skills still parse (Copilot CLI
  silently drops a skill whose frontmatter fails).

## Definition of Done

- Every acceptance criterion above is checked by the command it names.
- The regression test is proven RED by removing the rule, then restored.

## Notes

Filed after the operator asked whether the skills needed updating — they did, and
this is the gap `e668` left open. Sibling: `e668-b496-e264-4283` (CI gate sandbox).
Follow-on: a reusable `scripts/mutation_sandbox.py` CLI wrapper, which stacks on
`e668` and can then replace the inline invocation in the skill text.
